A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VRAdam optimizer and retain matching algorithms, experiments, and theoretical material. Their complete text, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original optimizer benchmarks and training-dynamics experiments in Sections 4–5, with results and multiple-run plots in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds LLM fine-tuning comparisons in Table 3 and a velocity-exponent ablation in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same moment estimates, clipped velocity-norm learning-rate gate, bias corrections, and AdamW update. Alternative velocity exponents are evaluated as ablations; they do not replace the proposed optimizer.

E1.justification: v3 adds OASST2 instruction following and GSM8K mathematical reasoning to the retained CIFAR-10, WikiText-2, GridWorld, and FineWebEdu-10B coverage. These fine-tuning tasks substantially extend evaluation beyond the previous language-modeling benchmarks.

E2.justification: Lion, previously only discussed in related work, is evaluated alongside AdamW in v3 Table 3. Original comparator sets remain unchanged. Although v3 also mentions Lion in the 124M pretraining paragraph, the corresponding Table 2 still reports only AdamW and VRAdam.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 4-bit NF4 QLoRA for LLaMA-2-7B and full-parameter GPT-2 Large fine-tuning, with perplexity, exact-match accuracy, and an instruction-quality score over 50 held-out instructions. Appendix D adds a separate 10-epoch CIFAR-10 exponent sweep at alpha_0 = 0.005. Previously reported splits, budgets, and settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests the choice of velocity-penalty exponent by comparing powers 2–6 on CIFAR-10. This is a targeted sensitivity analysis supporting the quartic-energy design. Existing training-dynamics analyses remain; replacing the all-NaN SGD plot with an equivalent statement does not remove its finding.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same seed disclosures, multiple-run error envelopes, and assertion of statistical significance. No new run counts, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are documented. The added LLM and ablation results are point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 Table 3 adds AdamW/VRAdam/Lion perplexities of 3.84/3.55/3.56 on OASST2 and 4.12/3.53/3.67 on GSM8K. Section 5 adds exact-match scores of 35% versus 42% and instruction-quality scores of 72.3 versus 78.5 for AdamW versus VRAdam. Table 4 adds exponent-ablation losses. Original benchmark values are unchanged after matching Tables 1–2 across versions. Section 4.1 also corrects the reported learning-rate trajectory to an initial decrease followed by an increase, matching the retained Figure 2.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds trajectory-level two-sided Hessian bounds and a nonconvex stability corollary using decoupled weight decay, while explicitly restricting the quadratic theorem to zero weight decay. v3 also corrects the CQLF feasibility inequality and the NRQCD second derivative in Appendix A. The stochastic convergence bound and its underlying proof remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding summary retain the same central claims: a physics-inspired AdamW modification, improved edge-of-stability behavior, the stated stochastic convergence rate, and broad benchmark superiority. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 argues for global scalar gating through rotation invariance and avoidance of switching instabilities. Appendix I explains feedback control versus schedule-free averaging and suggests their combination. Appendix C discusses omitted bias correction and weight decay. Section 5 interprets the new results as favorable scaling, and Section 7 replaces the explicit lack of experiments beyond 124M parameters with a generic compute limitation.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation citation and repository link, recommends alpha_1 = 10 alongside beta_3 = 1, and supplies some settings for the new experiments. Existing hyperparameter and hardware tables are largely unchanged. Detailed training recipes for the added LLM comparisons are not supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix I adds a focused comparison with Defazio et al.'s Schedule-Free optimizers. v3 also corrects the GFlowNet attribution to Bengio et al. and adds references supporting LLaMA, LoRA, and mechanics background. The main related-work organization and broader positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The explanatory treatment expands substantially through Appendix H's tutorial on phase space, Lagrangians, and Hamiltonians, Appendix I's mechanism comparison, and a dedicated global-versus-per-parameter subsection. Appendix B's prose is cleaned up, summary and future work are merged, and citation style, author text, and conference headers are updated.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reformats and enlarges the appendix plots, improving titles and axis labels, and adds panel letters to Figure 2. It adds two result tables and reorders the original benchmark tables. The all-NaN SGD language-modeling figure is replaced by text, while its finding and comparator participation are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added LLM benchmarks partly address v2's explicit 124M scaling limitation; the exponent ablation, formula corrections, clearer plots, and code pointer also add value. However, the new experiments lack detailed protocols and uncertainty reporting. The new nonconvex corollary extends global stability claims beyond the fixed-quadratic analysis without supplying a corresponding Lyapunov argument under the expanded assumptions. These empirical and explanatory gains coexist with insufficiently supported theoretical broadening, making the net quality direction uncertain.
